description: Status cards for real purchase orders: one host capture cycle of the purchase-order Portal relations (examples/po_status_host.live-check.json), then offline over those captures operating.status_card reads up to 10 purchase orders the investigator may read (plx.find on the type's display field) and computes each one's card by rule from plx.object, plx.process and plx.around (never a model guess): at most 5 ranked blockers (late, quantity mismatch, unpaid, not recorded, missing field, no need date), each cited with a next step naming a department, cited facts, one line for its copies in other systems and each unknown once. Passes with 10 cards, every one with at least one cited fact and none with an internal code (snake_case, a department code, an object id, a link type or a tool name) in its own words. Repeated for a reader without the purchase-order grant. Counts and enums only, never an identifier or value.
notes: Live-unverified until the live check runs it; the module test is injected-transport (operating/tests/test_status_card.py LiveCheckTest: the spec's own command over the order fixture's FakeWorkbench with ten purchase orders, the network refused, its expectations checked on the real summary; a Portal answering HTTP 500 at capture meets expect_blocked). Fewer than 10 readable purchase orders is a truthful red (below the minimum), never a pass. A card's facts are cited source values; blockers that rest on not finding a record say so ('not proof there is none'); the late verdict is plx.process po_delivery_window's own. Portal relations only in this cycle: BC lines and SharePoint or mailed confirmations reach the cards once their captures are added to the host config.
